note: No database, so database_rules does not apply. The model is called only server-side and no NEXT_PUBLIC env var exists, so no ai_browser_call. No .env file is committed because .gitignore covers .env*. CSS files, public SVGs, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING and GITHUB_SETUP were not reviewed. README demo scenario uses CUS-1002 while the admin page uses CUS-1015.

labels.what: 15 hardcoded sample orders used as the order system. All delivery dates are July and August 2026 and the window is 7 days, so every scenario is now denied, including the admin 'Successful refund' demo
15 fake customers with example.com emails and placeholder +91 phone numbers, used as the CRM
getCustomer tool reads the hardcoded customers array
getOrder tool reads the hardcoded orders array
getCustomerOrders tool filters the hardcoded orders array
processRefund is mock refund processing. It sets refundStatus on the in-memory order and returns a made-up REF-<timestamp> id. No payment provider is called and the state resets on restart
calculateRefund returns the full hardcoded order amount in INR. No real order or payment system, no partial refunds or fees
checkRefundEligibility runs real rule logic but only over the hardcoded customers and orders arrays
On a 429 or quota error runAgent silently swaps the model for runLocalAgent, a regex script that pulls CUS- and ORD- ids and runs the refund flow. The chat UI does not show which mode answered

Prompt says always run checkRefundEligibility first and never override the policy. processRefund never calls the eligibility check and takes no customerId, so a direct model call can refund Digital, Personalized, out-of-window or another customer's order. The tool description at tools.js line 210 repeats the rule only as text
Prompt says do not claim a refund was processed unless the refund tool confirms it. The final model text is returned as-is with no check against tool results
processRefund runs straight from a model tool call. No customer confirmation and no staff approval before the refund
Damaged products return eligible true with requiresVerification true. Nothing in the app reads requiresVerification, so the agent and the fallback refund damaged items with no verification step
Fallback agent processes the refund in the same turn the user types the ids, with no confirm step
processRefund checks amount above 0, amount not above the order total and not already refunded. It has no per-customer or per-session cap and no policy check, so one session can refund every order
POST /api/agent has no login. Anyone can trigger refunds and spend the OpenAI key
Customer identity is whatever CUS- id the user types. Nothing proves the requester owns the account, and ids are sequential, so any customer's order can be refunded
getCustomer and getCustomerOrders return a customer's name, email, phone and orders to anyone who names the id
Admin dashboard (Operations console) has no login. Its scenarios call /api/agent, and the success scenario processes a refund against the shared in-memory store
Decision falls back to scenario.expectedDecision when the API returns none. The OpenAI path always returns decision null, so the dashboard shows the scripted result
When the API call fails, the catch block shows the expected decision, so a failed run can display APPROVED
Refund mode shows refund.mode or 'Live'. The refund object never has a mode, so it always says Live, even for the local regex fallback
'System online' badge is static text with no health check
'Online' status in the chat header is static text with no health check

Two checkRefundEligibility functions disagree. The unused one here marks damaged items ineligible and rejects undelivered orders. The one the app uses in policy-validator.js marks damaged items eligible and has no not-yet-delivered check
Refund window of 7 days is hardcoded in the policy object, and '7' is repeated as literal text at line 9 and in the reason string at line 88
Non-refundable categories are hardcoded. README lists only Digital and Personalized
Currency 'INR' hardcoded here and at line 83
maxIterations 6 and model 'gpt-4o-mini' hardcoded
Client-supplied messages array is spread into the conversation with no role check. A caller can inject a system message or forge assistant and tool turns, such as a fake eligibility result
No rate limit and no size limit on the paid model endpoint. Each request can make up to 6 model calls
Raw error.message is returned to the client
Falls back to OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY for chat calls, an over-privileged key for this use
